summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The package declares a preinstall step (node setup.mjs) that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, unpacks it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to execFileSync a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with string-array rotation (function WV8StW rotating a >2000-entry mixed literal array n7gIxM) and hex/random identifier renaming — the payload that is auto-executed at install time is opaque. Using an alternate runtime (Bun) rather than the Node interpreter npm invoked causes the payload to bypass Node-based scanners at install. The package's package.json name is `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` while its description is `Verdocs Web SDK for React` and its dist code references https://api.verdocs.com, indicating the package impersonates the Verdocs SDK under an unrelated scope. A React SDK has no legitimate need to fetch and execute a second-language runtime against an obfuscated bundle at preinstall time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
